author: Mark Atwood
text:
Empirical check: serde_json::Error::Display does NOT include input data; it outputs 'EOF while parsing an object at line 1 column 24'-style strings. The concrete threat vector ('an attacker who can cause a parse failure gets a log-side data-leak channel') is closed by serde_json's own Display behavior.

The bead's broader principle still holds — MemoryError::Display interpolates self.0 verbatim, and a future call site that puts caller-controlled data into the inner String could leak it. But:

1. The proper fix is canonical-first: mail-server has the same Display shape (write!(f, 'MemoryBackend error: {}', self.description)) and needs the same sanitization audit.

2. The bead's recommended canary test (per JMAP-sc1b.79's per-type Debug-redaction pattern) requires changing Display semantics — either redacting at format time or dropping the inner content at construction. Neither is the simple e.to_string() substitution.

3. The fix interacts with JMAP-510h.36 (MemoryError(pub String) vs canonical's struct-with-description). Doing both together (also workspace-wide) would be cleaner.

Recommend folding this into the JMAP-xbeb workspace propagation epic alongside JMAP-510h.36, .39, .40, .44. The combined per-crate sweep would touch: MemoryError struct shape + Display sanitization + workspace-wide canary tests.

Until the human commits to that sweep, this bead is parked. The actual security exposure is bounded by serde_json's behavior; the .52 commit (b 10f1a61) already added operation context which is the diagnosability portion of the fix.
